newsitem.title: USA: Dlr longs bail at US noon, squeezed by trade talk.
newsitem.headline: Dlr longs bail at US noon, squeezed by trade talk.

text.p: The dollar was lower at noon, backpedalling from overnight gains as longs digested talk of renewed trade friction with Japan, dealers said.

Short-term funds were heavy sellers of dollar/mark and dollar/Swiss, traders reported. Dollar/yen also pulled back from an 11-week high near the key 118.95 level amid talk that U.S. auto makers were asking Washington to review Japanese trade barriers.
"The dollar is a little bit overbought and vulnerable to rumors. It's sitting at important levels across the board," said David Gilmore, a partner at Foreign Exchange Analytics.

Against the Swiss franc, the dollar was in retreat after touching 1.5261, the highest since August 1993, overnight. It was tending its wounds at the day's low on the mark, after an early stab at reclaiming Monday's 7-1/2 year high near 1.85.
At midday, dollar/mark was taking stock at 1.8347/57, compared to 1.8435/40 at the open and dollar/yen was trading at 118.22/32, down from 118.80/85.

Dollar/yen encountered stiff resistance after rising to 118.95 in early dealings on the back of reports showing Japanese industrial production fell 3.1 percent along with a 2.3 percent drop in retail sales in June.
Traders grew cautious in the run up to 119 yen, which denotes the 50-percent retracement of the dollar's high-low move from 127.47 to 110.62 this year.
A break 119 yen is expected to trigger another round of stop-loss buying but large offers reportedly lurked at 119.50.

A report from the Jiji news agency on Wednesday sparked debate on whether the car companies hoped to initiate proceedings under the Super 301 trade law, or had simply asked the the U.S. Trade Representative to review trade with Japan.
Either way, the dollar succumbed to profit-taking, dealers said.

"There was initial selling off of that Super 301 talk, out of Japan. Dollar/yen bounced back and now we seem to be offered again, it seems to be dollar selling across the board," said James Powers, a vice president of foreign exchange at Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale.
Traders said they quickly dismissed market rumors that Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin was considering resigning. They said such talk also weighed on the dollar in early trade.
The dollar shook off a report showing U.S. single family home sales rose 6.1 percent to an annual rate of 819,000 units in June. The number was close to forecasts of 818,000 units.
The dollar fell to 1.5153/58 Swiss from 1.5240/50 at the open and to Canadian $1.3810/15 from C$1.3830/35.
